title: ConvolutionFilter SWF flags: CLAMP/PRESERVE_ALPHA bits swapped vs Ruffle (bit0<->bit1)
description:
ConvolutionFilter (FilterID=5) flags byte has the CLAMP and PRESERVE_ALPHA bits SWAPPED relative to how Ruffle (the runtime) reads them. Same class of bug as the EditText flag-bit / ImportAssets2-reserved-byte risks: unit tests are green because they codify the encoder's (wrong) layout, but the runtime decodes the opposite.

OBSERVED (byte-proof via encodePlaceObject3WithFilters → manual decode mirroring ruffle/swf/src/read.rs read_convolution_filter):
  input  clamp=true,  preserveAlpha=false  → rawFlags=0x01 → Ruffle decodes clamp=FALSE, preserveAlpha=TRUE
  input  clamp=false, preserveAlpha=true   → rawFlags=0x02 → Ruffle decodes clamp=TRUE,  preserveAlpha=FALSE

SPEC / RUFFLE REFERENCE (ruffle/swf/src/types/convolution_filter.rs):
  bitflags ConvolutionFilterFlags {
    const CLAMP          = 1 << 1;   // bit 1
    const PRESERVE_ALPHA = 1 << 0;   // bit 0
  }
  read path: ruffle/swf/src/read.rs read_convolution_filter → ConvolutionFilterFlags::from_bits_truncate(read_u8).

ACTUAL ENCODER (packages/swf/src/filters.ts, writeConvolutionFilter):
    let flags = 0;
    if (f.clamp) flags |= 1;            // writes bit 0  -- WRONG, should be bit 1
    if (f.preserveAlpha) flags |= 2;    // writes bit 1  -- WRONG, should be bit 0
    bw.writeUI8(flags);

EXPECTED FIX:
    if (f.clamp) flags |= (1 << 1);          // CLAMP = bit 1
    if (f.preserveAlpha) flags |= (1 << 0);  // PRESERVE_ALPHA = bit 0

ALSO UPDATE THE STALE TEST that codified the wrong layout (it passes today against the wrong encoder, hence masked the bug):
  packages/swf/src/__tests__/convolution-filter.test.ts
    - header comment line ~12: "UI8: flags (bit 0 = clamp, bit 1 = preserveAlpha)"  -> swap
    - Test 6 (~line 162-190): the & 0x01 / & 0x02 assertions assert clamp on bit0 / preserveAlpha on bit1; flip to clamp on bit1 (0x02), preserveAlpha on bit0 (0x01).
  Also fix the layout comment in packages/swf/src/filters.ts writeConvolutionFilter docblock ("bit 0: clamp, bit 1: preserveAlpha").

IMPACT: a ConvolutionFilter (created via the model defaultConvolution / agent-MCP / FLA import path; encoder is wired through compiler/frames.ts + sprite.ts) renders in Ruffle with clamp and preserve-alpha inverted — out-of-bounds edge handling and alpha preservation behave backwards. Latent because the authoring-ui filter panel does not yet expose Convolution, but the model type, default factory, and encoder are all live.

SCOPE NOTE (separate, not this task): DisplacementMapFilter is emitted as FilterID=8, but Ruffle's read_filter has no case for 8 (`_ => Err("Invalid filter type")`), so any displacementMap filter makes Ruffle reject the entire FILTERLIST. That is an engine-support gap, not a flag-bit bug; flagged here for awareness only.

VERIFICATION DONE: all OTHER filter types byte-proofed CORRECT against Ruffle read order/flags at HEAD 3c9982c:
  DropShadow (inner/knockout/compositeSource=!hideObject/passes, color+blurXY+angle+distance FIXED16, strength FIXED8) OK;
  Glow (inner/knockout, compositeSource always set) OK;
  Bevel (highlight-then-shadow color order, inner+onTop from bevelType=full, knockout, passes 0xf) OK;
  GradientGlow & GradientBevel (numColors, colors[] then ratios[], inner/knockout/compositeSource/onTop, passes) OK;
  Blur (passes = bits 7-3) OK.
Only Convolution is defective.

Acceptance: swap the two bits in writeConvolutionFilter; update convolution-filter.test.ts to assert the Ruffle-correct layout (clamp=bit1, preserveAlpha=bit0); run pnpm --filter @flash/swf run test -- --run; golden-parity self-determinism unchanged.
